findings.description: The complete MODELINV ledger is passed to jq as a single --argjson argument. On Linux with 4 KiB pages, an individual argument cannot exceed approximately 128 KiB, regardless of available memory. A run whose serialized ledger exceeds that limit cannot produce its runs.jsonl row.
findings.failure_mode: Launching jq fails with 'Argument list too long'; set -e terminates the script before the result is written, losing the run's summary.
findings.suggested_fix: Load ledger data from a file using jq --slurpfile, or supply it through stdin instead of a command-line argument. Apply the same approach to other potentially large JSON inputs.

findings.description: In submodule mode every manifest path exists under .loa/<path> by construction (the manifest is generated from the upstream tracked tree), so the new `elif` branch makes the `Missing:` failure unreachable. Removing a mounted guard script or hook symlink from .claude/ is now reported only as an informational not-mounted count and never fails the integrity check, whereas before this change it was a hard failure.
findings.failure_mode: Tamper-by-deletion of a System Zone file in a submodule mount passes check-loa.sh with 'Integrity verified'-style output and exit 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish 'intentionally not linked' from 'was linked and removed' by consulting the mount's declared link scope (the set of paths the mount script creates) instead of treating any upstream-present path as benign; fail when a path in the declared scope is absent.

findings.description: Previously the function's last statement `[[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log ...` returned non-zero when drift was detected. The new unconditional `return 0` makes check_integrity succeed even after Tampered/Missing failures. Whether the overall exit code still reflects drift now depends entirely on `fail` tracking state globally; any caller that used the function's return status (e.g. `check_integrity || ...`) silently loses the signal.
findings.failure_mode: Integrity drift is printed but the script can exit 0 if the surrounding driver relied on the function's return code rather than a global error counter.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 1 when `drift` is true (`[[ "$drift" == "false" ]]` as the return expression, or explicit `if drift then return 1`), keeping not-mounted informational as intended.

findings.description: The entire MODELINV ledger (`$MINV`), pipeline.json, both dissent envelopes and the collected tool-write list are passed to jq as `--argjson` command-line arguments. Linux caps a single argv string at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128 KiB). A long multi-phase run with many Flatline voice rows in eval/model-invoke.jsonl can exceed this, at which point jq fails with 'Argument list too long' and, under `set -e`, the row is never written for exactly the long runs the harness is meant to measure.
findings.failure_mode: ablation-row.sh exits non-zero with E2BIG for large runs; runs.jsonl silently lacks those rows unless the batch runner handles the failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the large inputs to temp files and load them with `--slurpfile`/`--rawfile` (or pipe the MODELINV JSON on stdin) instead of `--argjson`.

findings.description: The header asserts the arm is never read from sandbox/ (DEC-0413), but `voices_run`, the DEGRADED/voice-shortfall `degraded` causes and `degraded_reason` are read from sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-{review,audit}.json, which is agent-writable during the run. An agent under test (or a prompt-injected one) can rewrite the envelope to report full voice completion and status OK, masking degraded gates in the measurement row.
findings.failure_mode: Ablation rows under-report degraded runs; comparisons between arms are skewed by sandbox-controlled data without any integrity check.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer the eval/ copy of the envelope (written by the harness outside the sandbox) and only fall back to sandbox/ with an explicit `envelope_source: sandbox` marker, or cross-check voices_run against MODELINV rows for the review/audit phases.

findings.description: The bats fallback is a hard-coded path under one operator's home (`~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats`). On any other host or CI runner that lacks bats on PATH this reads `bats=absent`, so the fingerprint differs between the operator's machine and every other host for the same toolchain, undermining the fingerprint's purpose of identifying identical environments.
findings.failure_mode: Runs on otherwise-identical toolchains produce different `host_fingerprint`/`image_digest` values depending on whose home directory the harness runs in.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the personal path; rely on PATH plus `LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN`/`--bats-bin`, and let `absent` be the honest value.
